claims.text: At tag stage-0 docs/craft/question-template.md gives a six-line form, in this order: Mục tiêu, Đã thử, Mong đợi, Thực tế, Môi trường, Tiếp theo.
The same file's Đã thử line asks for each attempt together with its result, and its Thực tế line asks for the error message verbatim ('nguyên văn').
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: docs/craft/question-template.md lines 7 and 9

claims.text: The same file states that finishing the first four lines often answers the question, because writing forces the asker to narrow the scope at the step they skipped.
The same file states that the last line turns the question into a decision: the reader knows the asker is not idle, and knows when to stop them.
Teams usually agree on a span, search alone inside it and ask when it ends; the same file names a cost on each side — too early disturbs someone else, too late loses your own day.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: docs/craft/question-template.md lines 42-44, section 'Hỏi khi nào' ('Đội thường thống nhất một khoảng thời gian')

claims.text: Stating the goal before the symptom lets a reader say the whole route is wrong instead of helping along the wrong route.
Listing attempts with their results tells a reader what is already ruled out, so they do not repeat the search the asker already did.
Expectation and actual result next to each other are what make a failure judgeable: the result alone says what happened, only the expectation says it was wrong.
A message carrying only the symptom forces any reply to start with a question of its own, which is why such a message can sit unanswered.
The text inside a picture is not text the reader can paste into a command as it stands, so they must retype or extract it; the picture also omits the goal, the attempts and the environment.
claims.source_hint: General property of an image versus text; claim limited to 'not pasteable as it stands' (text recognition can extract it).

claims.text: Writing the four lines does the same work the debugging loop of foundation.l2.debugging-method asks for — shrinking the distance between what you did and the first thing that was wrong — on paper rather than on a running command.
A filled-in question shows what you tried and what you already ruled out, so the reader sees method rather than a gap; a message with no attempts in it gives them nothing to see.
Waiting past the agreed span costs your own day, and the thing you are stuck on may be one the person beside you has already met.

127.0.0.1 is the address a machine uses for itself; a machine's ordinary name lookup reads the hosts file STAGE.md names before it asks DNS, and no DNS server the reader reaches knows donhang.local, so with no line there nothing on that machine gives the name an address.
claims.source_hint: refs/docker-docs engine/network (loopback); foundation.l1.dns §3 (hosts file before DNS); donhang.local gets an address only from STAGE.md's hosts line and docker-compose extra_hosts

claims.text: Set beside the attempts, the Môi trường line (the environment the attempts ran in) shows that every failed run was on the reader's own machine and browser and every run in the lab worked, which points at a step that machine needed.
